title: The life-stream
hookLine: the quiet stream of mind between active moments, and at rebirth

lines: BACK TO SLEEP UNDER THE TREE.
BETWEEN ONE THOUGHT AND THE NEXT.
cards: Yesterday's mango simile has one more step. After the man eats the fruit, he swallows the last of it, covers his head again, and goes back to sleep. That sleep matters.
Where does the mind go when nothing is striking a sense door, when you're deep in dreamless sleep, or simply between one thought and the next? It doesn't switch off.
The Abhidhamma says something keeps flowing underneath, quiet and steady, the way a river keeps moving under a frozen surface.

teach.b: The word is bhavanga, often translated the life-continuum, or the life-stream.
In the manual's picture, when no active process is running, the mind flows as bhavanga: moment after moment of a quiet, passive consciousness, with its own object, below anything you'd notice.
When a sound arrives, the stream vibrates and is interrupted, and an active process runs: turning, hearing, receiving, the javana moments, all of it.
Then the process ends, and the stream closes over again, like water after a stone. In deep dreamless sleep, the manual says, the mind is in bhavanga the whole time. There's more.
The manual teaches that the very first moment of a new life, the rebirth-linking consciousness, and the very last, the death consciousness, are of the same kind as the bhavanga in between.
So the quiet stream runs from a life's first moment to its last, holding the shape it was given at the start.
Isn't that a soul? The Abhidhamma's answer is no. Bhavanga isn't one thing that lasts.
It's a stream of moments, each arising and passing, each conditioning the next. A river has a shape and a direction, but no single drop is the river.

Some readers link bhavanga with a line in the Anguttara Nikaya that calls the mind luminous, stained by visiting defilements. The commentaries make that link, and teachers still discuss how far it goes.

how: Abhidhamma students learn bhavanga as the passive stream of consciousness between active processes and in dreamless sleep, and teachers in the Theravada tradition explain it as a stream of moments rather than a lasting self.

o: the deep focus reached in long meditation
a lasting soul that passes from life to life
the quiet stream of mind between active moments

p: first and last moments of a life

s: bhavanga is a soul that lasts through a life
it's a stream of moments, each arising and passing and conditioning the next.
in deep dreamless sleep, the manual says, the mind is in bhavanga
no active process is running, and the quiet stream flows.
the commentaries link bhavanga with a sutta line calling the mind luminous

games.q: you're deep in dreamless sleep. no sound, no dream, no thought. by the Abhidhamma's account, what is your mind doing?
o: flowing as bhavanga, the quiet stream
games.why: the mind doesn't switch off; it flows as bhavanga until something strikes a sense door.

practice: Let the breath find its own pace, and as thoughts come, neither chase them nor push them off; just watch for the end of one.
When a thought finishes, there may be a small gap before the next arrives, and you don't have to make it longer. Just notice it, the way you'd notice a pause in a conversation.

wordCard.voice: Bhavanga. The life-stream, the quiet mind that flows between active moments, in dreamless sleep, and from the first moment of a life to the last. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali: the life-continuum, the quiet stream of mind between active moments.

carryVoice: Your line: the quiet stream. A river has a shape, and no single drop is the river. See you tomorrow.
